body:
Tracked follow-up from TM-1 #425 dual re-audit (Auditor B finding TM1-B-1, P3). The P1 tautology was fixed and merged; this is the residual non-blocking nit.

## Context
`test/roman-coach-reviewed-migration.spec.ts:212-223` guards R76 §6 append-only migration ordering. Post-fix it correctly catches back-dating **below the floor** `FLOOR_TS=20261219000000` (independently injection-proven RED-when-injected / GREEN-when-clean, including an earliest-sorting evasion). Two residual gaps remain — both future-maintenance, neither a re-break:

1. **Scope gap:** a migration dated between FLOOR_TS and a later-landed slot (e.g. `20261219500000`, behind already-landed TM-1 `20261220000000`) stays GREEN. The guard anchors on the conv-review slot prefix, so it only catches reordering behind *that* slot, not behind every landed migration.
2. **Hardcoded `KNOWN_BELOW_FLOOR_COUNT = 146` footgun:** any legitimate future sub-floor migration forces a manual bump, and a maintainer could bump it to silence a genuinely back-dated dir. Inline comment warns against the latter (mitigates, doesn't prevent).

## Suggested hardening (future)
- Derive the guard from the full landed-migration max timestamp rather than a single floor prefix, so any new dir must sort after the current max.
- Replace the hardcoded count with a computed baseline (e.g. snapshot the set at a known-good SHA, or assert monotonic non-decreasing max prefix).

## Severity
P3 — the originally-reported back-dating attack is caught today. Future-maintenance footgun / narrow scope gap only. Filed to keep GitHub clean for the next operator (per standing rule). No blocker on TM-1 merge.

Origin: TM-1 #425, re-audit B report `tm1_reaudit_B.md`.
title: [P3] Harden R76 §6 append-only migration guard: floor-only scope + hardcoded count footgun (from TM-1 #425 re-audit)
